FOR IMMED IA TE RELEA SE June 11, 2026 Idaho an s So ur o n Risch, Trump , an d Iran , as A chilles Surges New Poll Shows Trump B elow 50%, Risch Underwater, and Voters Turning A gainst Continued Military A ction in Iran B OISE, Idaho . A new statewide survey conducted by the nonpartisan Bullfinch Group finds growing dissatisfaction among Idaho voters with their political leadership, including declining approval ratings for President Donald Trump and Senator Jim Risch, as well as rising opposition to ongoing U.S. military involvement in Iran.[ 1 ] The survey finds that Idahoans are now more likely to disapprove than approve of American military action in Iran, with 45% disapproving and 41% approving. This is in stark contrast to a previous May PPP poll showing Idahoans approving of the war 54%-38%. The results point to a rapid decline in support for the ongoing war, even in one of the nation’s most reliably Republican states. The poll also shows President Trump facing his weakest poll numbers in Idaho since returning to office. Just 48% of voters approve of Trump’s job performance, marking the first time his approval rating has fallen below 50% in statewide polling. The figure stands in sharp contrast to the 67% of the vote Trump received in 2024[ 2 ] . Senator Jim Risch’s numbers are even more troubling for the 3-term incumbent. Only 30% of Idahoans approve of Risch’s job performance, while 39% disapprove, leaving him even more underwater than he was in March. In an attempt to counter-message this growing reality, Risch yesterday released a Peak Insights poll showing him winning 55% of voters.[ 3 ] Peak Insights, formerly known as Moore Information Group and run by a former Montana Republican Party chair[ 4 ] , is a dedicated Republican pollster whose work has been shown to have below-average quality and a pronounced Republican bias.[ 5 ] Campaign manager Austen Campbell comments “ This 55% is strikingly low for a 3-term Senator from a very red state, in a push poll released in June. Why is Risch releasing a push poll in June?” Greg Casey, a long-term Republican strategist now consulting with the Achilles campaign, called the Risch poll bogus. “Polling can be manipulated. It’s an old political trick used by unscrupulous consultants[ 6 ] . Only ask those you think support your position. If your main phone is mobile, were you even a part of the poll? It’s an act of desperation typical of Risch’s Las Vegas consultant.” “These numbers [in the Bullfinch poll] tell a clear story,” said Independent candidate Todd Achilles. “Idahoans are frustrated with Washington’s direction, deeply worried about the cost of living, and rightfully unhappy with continued military involvement overseas. With Jim Risch getting 88.26% of his campaign funding from out of state[ 7 ] it’s no wonder Idahoans are looking for new independent leadership that will actually put Idaho first.” The Bullfinch Group survey was conducted among registered Idaho voters and highlights growing volatility beneath the surface of Idaho politics, with declining support for both the president and the state’s senior senator alongside rising demand for accountability and change.

A B OUT TOD D A C HILLES Todd Achilles, 58, is an Army veteran, former state legislator, public policy professor, and business executive. He grew up on a family farm, served as a U.S. Army tank commander and armor officer, spent over 20 years in senior leadership roles at T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard, and several technology startups, and served in the Idaho House of Representatives before resigning in July 2025 to launch his U.S. Senate campaign. He lives in Boise with his family. Achilles has spent the past 11 months campaigning across Idaho, visiting all 44 counties and participating in more than 130 public events. More information can be found at achillesforidaho.com.
